correctness.rationale: The defining Euclidean clearance is the minimum unit-normal slack min_i(h_i-u_i·x). Coarea on unique-minimizer regions gives density f_{T,J=i}(t)=A_i(t)/Vol(P), including a canonical continuous density-level conditional probability. At one interior shell, all q_i(t0)=q_i(0) force positive proportional facet areas A_i(t0)=s^{d-1}A_i(0). Both polytopes have the same outward facet-normal surface-area measures after scaling. Minkowski surface-area uniqueness implies P_t0=w+sP; volume/proper inclusion yields s<1, and support comparisons construct a ball tangent to all original facets. Weighted normal equilibrium ∑A_i(0)u_i=0 proves maximality of its radius. Converse is explicit inner homothety and Beta(1,d) clearance. The untested augmented-normal linear system enforces the sparse condition, and any three distinct normal points on the circle are non-collinear. Independent direct shell calculations reproduce square/triangle constancy versus rectangular deviations. This is an infinite proof with finite diagnostics.

final_claim: For any full-dimensional Euclidean polytope in dimension d>=2, independence of clearance T and closest facet J, equality of all relative inner-offset facet areas at any one positive t<inradius, and existence of a common inball tangent to all facets are equivalent. A subset test suffices whenever the untested augmented facet normals (1,u_j) are linearly independent; for any convex quadrilateral a single named edge is sufficient.
limitations: Convex Euclidean polytope and continuous density-level conditioning; no nonconvex bodies, finite-sample stability, or arbitrary single facet in high dimension.
